Ethan B.: heads up — our quickstart sample app typechecks fine locally but fails for Next Edge deploys. users hit: "No overload matches this call" when calling createClient<>.
Ethan B.: repro: Next 13 Edge API route, import: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` then `const client = Redwood.createClient({})` — tsserver shows overload problem.
Rosa M.: this smells like a typing + moduleResolution mismatch. what are the sample app tsconfig + package.json exports?
Ethan B.: sample app tsconfig uses defaults from next, basically `moduleResolution: node`, no esModuleInterop. package.json of SDK has `type: "module"` and conditional exports for import/require but types is a single dist/types/index.d.ts.
Jin W.: single d.ts + conditional esm export can confuse TS in edge bundles. TS 4.9+ supports `exports.types` but only if you publish those files. Edge toolchains (Vercel/bun/deno) often prefer pure ESM and ignore CJS paths, so they might resolve a different set of declarations.
Sam R.: concrete suggestion we used elsewhere: 1) switch factory to named export signatures and export default the named symbol. e.g. `export function createClient<T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(opts: Opts): Client<T>; export default createClient;` this avoids `typeof import("...").default` confusion.
Ethan B.: we currently have two overloads with `T = any`. could `any` be making inference pick the wrong overload in some consumers?
Rosa M.: yes. `any` disables inference signals. replace with `T extends object = {}` or `T = never` patterns. or make overloads more distinct: one signature `createClient<T>(opts: Opts): Client<T>` and the second `createClient<T, H extends Hooks<T>>(opts: Opts & { hooks: H }): Client<T>` so they don't overlap. small discriminator helps TS pick the right overload.
Jin W.: also try `unknown` vs `any`: prefer `unknown` constrained like `T extends Record<string, unknown>`. `unknown` forces consumers to be explicit and reduces accidental overload matching.
Sam R.: for package.json, add conditional types: `{ ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs", "types": "./dist/types/esm/index.d.ts" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }` so modern resolvers pick the right d.ts. Publish both `dist/types/esm` and `dist/types/cjs` if you need parity.
Ethan B.: build change is annoying but doable. any faster workaround for existing release?
Rosa M.: include an example tsconfig in README for sample app consumers: `{"compilerOptions": {"moduleResolution": "bundler", "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true}}` and suggest `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` as the safer import on edge.
QA-bot: opened issue #1352: "sdk: edge quickstart typecheck failure - overload resolution" assigned to @ethanb
Ethan B.: I'll do a small PR: 1) change overload defaults to constrained unknowns, 2) add named exports + default wrapper, 3) add conditional types entry and publish both d.ts trees, 4) update quickstart README with tsconfig snippet.
Sam R.: add a CI job that `npm pack` the package, extract, and run `tsc --build` on the sample consumer using nodeNext and bundler configs. catches regressions.
Jin W.: also add a tiny test that imports via both `import Redwood from` and `import { createClient }` to ensure both forms typecheck.
Ethan B.: thanks — will send draft PR and a follow-up with repro repo. ETA tomorrow AM.
Rosa M.: thanks — will review the declaration outputs. :+1:
Sam R.: :rocket:
